title: Edge-coupled stripline on a board: two 2.4 mm traces 0.6 mm apart on the inner layer of a 3 mm εr = 2.2 board between its ground planes (the region's lid and floor), meshed by the planar mesher: the even and odd modes' impedances
source: Cohn's exact conformal mapping of zero-thickness coupled strips between infinite planes: Z0e = η0/(4√εr) K(ke′)/K(ke), ke = tanh(πW/2b) tanh(π(W + S)/2b), Z0o alike with ko = tanh(πW/2b) coth(π(W + S)/2b) (S. B. Cohn, Shielded coupled-strip transmission line, IRE Trans. MTT 3(5):29–38, 1955), K by the arithmetic–geometric mean (emcraft-theory::coupled::z0_even_odd, evaluated apart from the solver). The two TEM modes share β = k0 √εr, so any combination is a mode; the ports split them along the line's impedance matrix (power-orthogonal, orthogonal currents: equal currents on the strips, then opposite ones), each mode's impedance per conductor 2P/Σ|I|²

quantities.quantity: the first port mode's impedance at 2 GHz, the even mode (Ω)
quantities.reason: −0.22 % measured: 1 mm triangles graded to 50 µm at the traces' edges, cells across the substrate graded towards the copper, side walls three spacings away where Cohn's planes are infinite

quantities.quantity: the second port mode's impedance at 2 GHz, the odd mode (Ω)
quantities.reason: −0.53 % measured: the odd mode's field crowds into the 0.6 mm gap, which the size field's growth away from the edges (half the distance) crosses in a few triangles; 25 µm at the edges gives −0.45 %
